question: A particular sum of money is lent at Simple Interest for 3 years. However, when the same sum of money is lent at a rate 5% p.a. higher than the previous rate, fetches Rs 1080 more. The money lent out originally was:
solution:
Formula:

SI = (P x R x T) ÷ 100

Where-

P = Principal amount

R = Rate

T = Time

SI = Simple Interest

Calculation:

Let the Original sum be Rs 100 and the rate of interest be "r%"

⇒ SI = 100 × 3 × r over 100 = 3r

SI under rate 5% higher than the previous rate = 100 × 3 × (r+5) over 100 = 3r + 15

⇒ Difference = 3r + 15 - 3r = 15

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9c24130a9b471e28373099ac39e718410217373fdfa803941b286381712f0fa9.png] 

∴ Original principal = 1080 × 100over15 = Rs 7200

**The money lent out originally was Rs 7200.**
